title: National coordination of contract teachers’ demonstrations in Casablanca and Inezgane
organizer: National Coordination of Teachers Forced to Contract (CNECC); the local report also notes support from education unions and civic organizations
participants_original: The opened Arabic weekly describes sizable attendance and a mass sit-in in Inezgane but gives no count. A search-only result reports hundreds across Casablanca and Inezgane.
threshold_50_evidence: Qualitative “mass”/“sizable attendance” wording in the opened Arabic weekly supports a likely threshold, but there is no numerical or per-city count; “hundreds” is available only in a search-result snippet. Retained pending threshold confirmation.

start_date.summary: Both reports identify teacher actions/march on 26 January 2021; the local weekly names Casablanca and Inezgane.

location.summary: The local weekly identifies Casablanca and Inezgane.

organizer.summary: The National Coordination of Teachers Forced to Contract organized the action; education unions and civic groups are described as supporters.

demands.summary: Teachers defended public education and opposed contract employment, seeking public-service integration and a government/education ministry dialogue.

state_target.summary: The stated demands address the Moroccan government and Ministry of Education.

participants.summary: The opened source uses qualitative “sizable attendance”/“mass sit-in” language for Inezgane; a search-only report says hundreds across two cities. Neither establishes each city’s count.

threshold_50.summary: Likely at least 50 based on the opened “mass sit-in” wording; the numerical corroboration remains search-only.

state_response.summary: The local weekly says security forces were deployed to prevent the Inezgane gathering, but teachers ultimately held a sit-in. Search-only reports say Casablanca authorities banned the planned march; no other response is established.

notes: A local weekly reports that the Jan 26 action occurred despite a reported Casablanca ban. The one-day coordinated action is represented as a single multi-location candidate because the same national coordination and demands are documented; whether this is the correct event unit remains reviewable.
open_questions: Turnout by city and the basis for the search-only “hundreds” estimate
Whether force was used against participants at each location
Continuity of the teachers’ campaign before and after January
Whether one national multi-location record best follows the original event rule
